nominal_help.text: Preserve every disjunctive noun phrase, including sisters, and both the hundredfold requital and additional eternal-life clauses. Kinship morphology is not interchangeable: complete sweostor system is now taught; earlier brōðor/mōdor systems remain distinct.
Strǣt has the public-place sense explicitly in Cook’s English glossary59 and Reader vocabulary314. This is a new sense alongside prior street.
Tīd hour is promoted from the previously supplied Unit13 interval sense. Exact sixth/ninth ordinal words and temporal ymbe are handled in the grammar support.

Ǣfen evening and wyrhta workman are prior nouns. Gerēfa steward and wīngeard vineyard have complete new tables; mēd gains the wage/hire sense. The evening-become expression needs separate construction support.
Hęfignessa is accusative plural burdens. Hǣte is the selected dative singular heat after on. The abstract hǣtu/hǣlu discussion must not manufacture plural count uses.

Hǣlu salvation is selected invariant singular; earlier hǣle is a recognized oblique variant. If unnan is used, its grant construction governs genitive of the thing: the possessive must be genitive ðīnre, even though invariant hǣlu looks unchanged.
Use prior setl seat/throne. Preserve the source hint fōtsceamul: complete selected cells retain -sceamul-. Hierusalem is a supplied proper-name form; no full foreign-name declension is inferred.
Hēafod loses unstressed o before endings (hēafd-); hǣr has heavy-neuter zero plural. The final component, not the long first component fōt-, controls retention in fōtsceamul.
The printed word is earth, not oath. There is no source emendation.

Either prior gedeorf labor with an explicitly licensed from relation or the source’s æt ðīnum gewinne frame requires its own final grammar binding. Reader161.5 and note6 directly support æt = from; this is evidence outside the assigned reading span.

Brȳd is feminine; selected accsg brȳde follows Cook51b. Hām here is a noun with accusative object function, distinct from prior adverb hām homewards. Preserve the printed blōstmian hint, matching the selected blossom lemma.
Ālīesend is productive as the singular Redeemer title. Its plural morphology is reference only and does not assign a theological plural sense.

Dęne and Engle have complete plural-only lexical scope. Lēoðwyrhta is a weak masculine poet; āwęndednes is the -nes translation noun, with doubled ss in inflected forms. Lædene is a supplied dative language name.

Bēcrǣding was earlier supplied only; it now has a complete table with productive singular reading and reference-only plurals. The twelve-years-old phrase remains explicitly bounded higher-number syntax.

Bōc has bēc in genitive/dative singular and nominative/accusative plural; bōc remains accusative singular. Lēoða is genitive plural poems. Do not make the supplied whichever-of-two clause a blanket productive case-attraction rule.

policy: Nominal notes supplement visible vocabulary and full tables. They do not silently alter an English prompt or authorize unsupported verb systems.
